kurz: Why a euro today and a euro in ten years' time are different quantities, what interest is made up of, and where the line runs between saving, investing and speculating.

bloecke.md:
A twenty-euro note is printed cotton paper with a security thread. Its value rests on the expectation that others will continue to accept it in future as payment for work, goods or services. Money is therefore a **claim on future goods**. How much you get for it depends on prices at the time of purchase, and those prices change.

A sum of money therefore always comes with a point in time. €1,000 today and €1,000 in ten years cannot be compared directly, in the same way that 100 kilometres and 100 kilometres per hour are different quantities. A comparison that ignores the point in time leads to wrong decisions, and does so systematically in favour of the distant payment, whose amount looks larger than its value today would justify.
Money is a claim on future goods. Its value depends on what you get for it and at what point in time, and not on the nominal amount alone.

## The components of interest

Anyone who lends or invests money gives up something certain, namely immediate command over purchasing power. In return, they receive the promise of a later payment. The price of this exchange is interest. It is made up of three components, none of which is shown separately on any account statement:

- **Time preference** describes the fact that people would rather consume now than later. Compensation is therefore demanded for waiting, even when there is no risk.
- **Inflation compensation** takes rising prices into account. For purchasing power to stay the same, the amount repaid has to be correspondingly larger. What matters here is expected future inflation, not past inflation.
- The **risk premium** has two sources. The first is *default risk*, the danger that the debtor does not pay. The second is the [[Term premium|term premium]] for tying up the money. An investor who locks up their money for ten years cannot react to interest rates that rise in the meantime and bears the risk that inflation picks up.

The three components cannot be observed directly, but their sum can. It rises visibly with maturity and risk.

bloecke.titel: Interest rates by maturity and risk, September 2026
bloecke.unter: Three interest rates from the same week, in the same currency and under the same legal system, whose differences arise from maturity and risk.

bloecke.md:
The central bank's overnight rate and the yield on the ten-year German federal bond are 1.02 percentage points apart. Both debtors are considered first-class. The gap is therefore almost entirely compensation for tying up money for ten years. The statutory default interest rate (Verzugszins) is a further three percentage points higher. Under Section 288 BGB (Civil Code), it is five percentage points above the basic rate of interest (Basiszinssatz), which has stood at 1.52% since 1 July 2026. In this way, the legislature, too, puts a price on time and on broken promises to pay. A debtor who pays late is drawing on credit from the creditor that the creditor has not agreed to.

The central bank sets only the short-term rate. The 3.52% rate on the ten-year Bund is set by the market on the basis of expectations about inflation, growth and risk. In 2026, long-term rates have risen more than key interest rates. The central bank and the capital market therefore set interest rates independently of each other.

In September 2026, the ECB pays 2.50% on deposits, while German consumer prices in August were 2.9% higher than in the same month a year earlier. The [[Real interest rate|real interest rate]] is therefore negative, at around minus 0.4 percentage points. That already applies to investors who receive the full central bank rate. Banks pass on changes in key interest rates with a delay and only partially, and usually none of it reaches the current account. The return of interest therefore does not yet mean a gain in purchasing power.

## Loss of purchasing power on account balances

A balance that earns no interest loses [[Purchasing power|purchasing power]] to the same extent that prices rise. Within a single year the loss is barely noticeable, but over a decade it is, for many households, the largest single item in their financial lives. It is also the only item that arises without any transaction being booked. Because the account balance stays the same, the loss appears neither on any statement nor as a debit.

bloecke.titel: Purchasing power of €10,000 in a non-interest-bearing account
bloecke.unter: Calculated using the official German annual inflation rates, with an account balance that stays unchanged at €10,000 every year.

bloecke.md:
At the end of 2015, €10,000 is placed in a non-interest-bearing account. The German annual inflation rates for the years 2016 to 2025 are 0.5 / 1.5 / 1.8 / 1.4 / 0.5 / 3.1 / 6.9 / 5.9 / 2.2 / 2.2%. For each year, purchasing power is divided by the factor for that year's rate:

`10,000 ÷ (1.005) ÷ (1.015) ÷ … ÷ (1.022) = €7,751`

The loss of purchasing power is €2,249, around 22% in ten years, even though no money is withdrawn. The three years from 2021 to 2023 alone brought a combined 16.7% inflation. At the end of 2025, the German price level stands about 22% above its 2020 level. This increase remains in place when the inflation rate falls, because a falling rate only means that prices are rising more slowly.

Savers with interest-bearing balances lost less purchasing power, but only rarely none at all. The ECB deposit facility rate stood at minus 0.50% from September 2019 to July 2022 and did not reach 2.50% again until February 2023. By then, the price level had already risen by around 15% compared with 2020. Attractive interest rates on savings therefore only appeared once the period of high price increases was largely over. This time lag is the rule, because central banks raise interest rates in response to inflation, that is, with a delay.

## Saving, investing and speculating

In everyday language the three words are often used interchangeably, but they describe different activities.

**Saving** means postponing consumption and keeping purchasing power for later. The amount is preserved in nominal terms and is available at short notice. Saving does not reliably deliver a real gain, because over long periods the real return on bank deposits and the money market is close to zero.

**Investing** means entrusting capital to someone who uses it to produce something, such as a company, a government or a landlord. The return comes from the value this debtor creates, in the form of interest, profits or rents. It does not depend on someone paying a higher price later.

**Speculating** means betting on a price change without any ongoing income behind it. A profit arises only if a later buyer pays more. Speculation is not disreputable and serves a function in the market. For all participants taken together, however, it is a zero-sum game before costs.

In 1934, Benjamin Graham distinguished between investment and speculation by the method used, regardless of the product. By his definition, an investment operation rests on thorough analysis and promises safety of the capital invested and an adequate return. Everything else he classed as [[Speculation|speculation]].

bloecke.text: promises safety of principal and an adequate return
bloecke.quelle: Benjamin Graham / David Dodd, Security Analysis (1934), on the distinction between investment and speculation

bloecke.md: It follows that the same share, the same fund or the same house can be an investment or a speculation, depending on what the expectation is based on. A world ETF bought for thirty years is an investment. The same world ETF is a speculation if it is bought on Monday because a central bank meeting is due on Thursday.

bloecke.md:
## Where returns come from

The saying that money “works” is imprecise, because returns are generated by people, machines, patents and land. Providers of capital give others the means for this work and receive a share of the result in return. The return is this share, and because the result is not fixed in advance, the provider of capital bears a risk. Without a productive process, a return can only come from money that previously belonged to someone else. This line of reasoning can be used to test any offer that promises high interest at low risk.

Over very long periods, the results of the three approaches differ fundamentally.

bloecke.titel: Real return per year, world market, 1900 to 2024
bloecke.unter: After deducting inflation and before costs and taxes; source: Dimson/Marsh/Staunton, Global Investment Returns Yearbook 2025.

bloecke.titel: The same data as final values
bloecke.md: A dollar invested in US equities in 1900 was worth $124,854 in nominal terms at the end of 2025, $284 in long-term government bonds and $69 in the money market. Over the same period, the price index rose 38-fold. In real terms, that corresponds to multiples of 3,296, 7.5 and 1.8. In the money market, purchasing power has therefore not even doubled in 126 years.

The 5.2% is an average over 125 years that included long periods without any real gain. US equities returned minus 0.8% a year in real terms from 1966 to 1981, and also minus 0.8% from 2000 to 2012. Worldwide, the real return on equities from 2000 to 2024 was 3.5% instead of 5.2%. The equity premium over the money market was 4.3 percentage points, so the money market works out at minus 0.8% in real terms over these 25 years. Planning based on long-term averages must therefore allow for a range of possible outcomes, since no particular value is guaranteed.

## The six quantities of this module

The remaining lessons of the module cover calculations that determine the value of an amount falling due at a different point in time. Interest and [[Compound interest|compound interest]] carry an amount today forward into the future, and present value discounts a future amount back to today. Return measures the result, and risk describes its possible dispersion. Inflation and costs are the two deductions that always apply. Inflation is not shown on any statement, and costs depend on your own choices.

bloecke.unter: The top row shows the three quantities that determine the effective rate, the middle the calculation from today's value to the future value, and the bottom the calculation back via inflation and present value.

bloecke.md: Before assessing a product, you should be clear about when the money will be needed and what it should be able to buy at that point. Most other decisions follow from this. Money needed in the short term does not belong in volatile investments, and money that will not be needed for thirty years does not belong in a bank account.

mitnehmen: A sum of money is only complete, and comparable with other amounts, once the point in time is stated.
Interest is compensation for waiting, expected inflation and risk, and therefore rises measurably with maturity and probability of default.
A positive interest rate does not automatically mean a positive real return, because with a deposit facility rate of 2.50% and inflation of 2.9%, a balance loses purchasing power.
€10,000 left in an account without interest from the end of 2015 to the end of 2025 had the purchasing power of €7,751 at the end, although nothing was withdrawn.
Whether something is saving, investing or speculating depends on where the expected return is supposed to come from, and not on the product.

begriffe.text: The tendency to value consumption today more highly than the same consumption later. It explains why interest is demanded even with complete certainty and no inflation.

The additional interest paid for tying up capital for a long time. It compensates for the fact that the investor cannot react to interest rates that rise in the meantime and bears the inflation risk over the entire term.
The nominal interest rate minus the inflation rate. It shows how purchasing power changes. With interest at 2.50% and inflation at 2.9%, it is around minus 0.4 percentage points.
The quantity of goods that a sum of money can buy at a given point in time. It is the relevant measure of wealth; the nominal amount alone says little about it.

A transaction whose expected return comes solely from a future price change and not from ongoing value creation. According to Graham, speculation is anything that does not combine thorough analysis, safety of principal and an adequate return.
